model_output.score_comment_short: Several recent bullets quantify workloads, though results and marketing authority remain unclear.
model_output.score_comment_long: Posting frequency, product-copy volume, and property-record volume make the work concrete. The marketing title suggests broader responsibility than the listed duties explain. Add your actual decisions and responsibilities to the relevant bullets.
model_output.score_plain: The workload figures help a reviewer understand what you handled. For broader marketing roles, the resume leaves questions about your authority and results.
model_output.first_impression: Your recent marketing role combines Instagram, website copy, order packing, and customer emails. The director title stands out, but the bullets don't yet explain whether the role included broader marketing decisions.
model_output.biggest_gap_example: "Flagged missing documents for the closing team" doesn't say what you did after flagging them, so your part in the closing process is difficult to judge.
model_output.summary: Writing descriptions for 40 candle scents gives a reviewer a concrete sense of your website content work. Alongside regular Instagram posting, it points to hands-on marketing and customer-facing work rather than an explicitly described department leadership role. Earlier, you entered property records and flagged missing documents for a closing team. The resume doesn't establish whether you set marketing priorities or supervised others, which matters when comparing the director title with the work described.
strengths: The Instagram bullet gives both a posting range and follower count, helping a reader understand the account you worked on.
Entering 150 property records a day makes the volume of your data entry work tangible.
Training 4 new baristas shows you had a role in teaching others, even though the resume doesn't describe formal supervision.
gaps: The candle company's marketing bullets don't describe how content was planned or selected, leaving your decision-making role unclear.
No result is stated for the website copy or Instagram work, so a reader cannot tell what changed after publication.
The skills list doesn't connect Canva, Shopify, or Excel to particular tasks, making it difficult to assess how you used them.
